description.narrative: Contribute to the consolidation of social and political conditions for peacebuilding, through progress in equality and realization of rights and consolidation of right-holders as social actors for peace.

Syftet med insatsen är att bidra till villkoren för en stabil och varaktig fred i Colombia med ett nationellt, territoriellt och rättighetsbaserat perspektiv. Programmet får 63,8 MSEK från Sidas finansiering mellan 2017-2021.

The objective of the contributin is to contribute to the conditions of a stable and lasting peace in Colombia with a national, territorial, and rights-based perspective. The program will receive 63,8 MSEK of Sida funding between 2017-2021.

During the project period, Diakonia and its partners achieved important results (both related to approved work plans and unexpected ones mainly related to context-response interventions), while also being affected by challenges associated with the pandemic during 2020 and 2021. During 2020, aside from the limitations that Diakonia faced to conduct field visits due to mandatory confinement, partners, human rights defenders, and social leaders faced increasing levels of violence, including threats, harassment, confinements, and murders, and often placing them under serious economic hardship.
Furthermore, dialogue with local and national authorities has been more challenging, as they are unwilling to entertain these spaces with civil society organisations despite often being legally mandated. This is also tied to the reluctance to ensure the adequate implementation of the Peace Agreement.
Despite the difficulties in 2020, Diakonia and its partners were able to withstand and contribute to objectives defined in the project plan. Diakonia was very flexible in adapting to the COVID-19 particularities and very early into the pandemic, Diakonia embraced the concept of virtual missions to the territory. This was very important, because monitoring, follow-up, and observation of the international community has a great impact in providing an element of safety to the affected communities. Moreover, Diakonia considers that albeit the impact of the pandemic on their local partners, placing additional efforts into addressing and supporting marginalised social and ethnic groups had a positive risks and damage mitigation effect.
Diakonia's partners' ability to adapt to the COVID-19 challenges was also something that was positively highlighted. They demonstrated an immense amount of creativity and innovation to continue working despite the pandemic-related obstacles. A few noteworthy initiatives included virtual psychosocial support to female victims of gender-based violence (which was heightened during the pandemic), digital education for rural schooling, collective protection methods spearheaded by the indigenous guard, and an online e-commerce platform for female entrepreneurs.
Another positive accomplishment during the project has been the Open Fund for Initiatives for Peace, Human Rights and Gender Equality. The fund has offered Diakonia an opportunity to expand its work within new territories, new processes, strengthen topics of interest such as gender and gender diversities, and increase its work with the institutions of the Transitional Justice System created by the Peace Agreement.
It is Diakonias assessment that the Fund is a powerful tool to respond with high levels of flexibility, strategic contextual needs, and redirect efforts towards crucial projects or processes that require the catalytic type of assistance offered by the Fund. One key project Diakonia has highlighted is the close work with female magistrates of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (Spanish acronym JEP) on sexual violence within the armed conflict.
Overall, Diakonia expressed pride in their partners' commitment within monitoring and working towards the human rights situation in their respective territories.
